title: Agent Persistence Schema for Simulated Minds
description: SQLite schema for agent identity, state, and event history. Version 1.0. Separate from concept dreaming tables — same DB file, different writer scripts, no foreign-key coupling.

agents.description: Registered simulated agents. One row per agent per world.

world_id.description: FK to world-spec or simulation instance

entity_type.description: NPC, creature, object, system, observer, etc.

agents.sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agents (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, world_id TEXT NOT NULL, entity_type TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, created TEXT NOT NULL, last_updated TEXT NOT NULL)

agent_state.description: Current state snapshot per agent. One row per agent — upserted on each state write. The state_json is the canonical JSON blob for the agent's current runtime state.

state_json.description: JSON blob of current agent state (position, inventory, mood, flags, etc.)

tick.description: Monotonic tick counter for this agent

agent_state.sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agent_state (agent_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, state_json TEXT NOT NULL, tick INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, written_at TEXT NOT NULL)

agent_history.description: Append-only event log per agent. Immutable — never updated, only inserted. Full replay from history reconstructs any past state.

event_type.description: spawn, move, interact, observe, tick, die, etc.

agent_history.sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agent_history (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, agent_id TEXT NOT NULL, event_type TEXT NOT NULL, event_json TEXT NOT NULL, tick INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, written_at TEXT NOT NULL)

privacy_floor.rule: No PII, credentials, or client data in agent state. Agent state is simulated world data only.
privacy_floor.enforced_by: agent-state.js writer script — validates state_json against privacy markers before write

coexistence.rule: Agent tables coexist in memory.sqlite alongside memories, concepts, and associations tables. No foreign keys between agent and concept tables. Separate writer scripts: agent-state.js (incremental append/upsert) vs build-memory-db.js (scratch rebuild).

writer_determinism: Same input at same tick → same state_json hash. Node stdlib only, no randomness, no external API calls.
